papers.title: Selection of Best Reserves Estimation Methodology to Quantify and Reduce the Uncertainty – Accompanied by Çayirdere Gas Field Case Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Uncertainty in reserves estimation plays a critical role at all-time steps of production/development plans and determines the financial strength of the project and the company. In this study, the importance of probabilistic approach to reserves estimation is emphasized by showing change in the estimated values of reserves with producing time. An analytic uncertainty propagation method (AUPM), a simple, yet quite accurate alternative uncertainty quantification method to the well-known Monte Carlo method, is used to assess the uncertainty in gas reserves estimations. In addition to the theory, as a case study, one of the largest Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) gas field, Çayırdere Field, reserves is estimated, and uncertainties for this field reserve are presented at all-time steps. As a result, the estimated value of the most likely reserve (P50) by utilization of AUPM in conjunction with probabilistic methodology prior to production period, matches quite well with the value estimated at the abandonment of the reservoir by using performance-based methods. The Çayırdere Gas Field Case Study supports the glorious success of the approach promised in this study.

summary_en.motivation: Uncertainty in gas reserve estimation critically impacts project economics, necessitating efficient quantification methods.
summary_en.method: An analytic uncertainty propagation method (AUPM) is applied as a simple yet accurate alternative to Monte Carlo simulation for reserve estimation.
summary_en.result: The P50 reserve estimated by AUPM before production closely matches the value determined by performance-based methods at abandonment.
summary_en.validation: The method is validated through a case study of the Çayırdere gas field, demonstrating its accuracy over the field's lifetime.

papers.title: Influence of PBL teaching method on active learning and teaching satisfaction of nursing students
papers.abstract:
Objective
To investigate the PBL teaching method on active learning and teaching satisfaction of the nursing train.


Methods
A total of 40 cases of nursing graduating interns entered our department internship were randomly divided into the experimental group and the control group, 20 cases in each group, the control group was received the traditional clinical teaching method, the observation group were given PBL teaching method, the enthusiasm for learning and teaching satisfaction were compared.


Results
The autonomous learning, active participation, mutual communication, critical thinking and other aspects of the learning initiative in the experimental group were higher than those in the control group(P< 0.05). The satisfaction degree of comprehensive ability, knowledge, teaching attraction, interactive in the experimental group were higher than those in the control group(P< 0.05).


Conclusions
PBL teaching method is helpful to improve students'initiative and teaching satisfaction.


Key words: 
PBL teaching; Nursing students; Active learning; Teaching satisfaction

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the effect of problem-based learning (PBL) on nursing students' active learning and teaching satisfaction.
summary_en.method: A randomized controlled trial with 40 nursing interns divided into PBL and traditional teaching groups, comparing learning initiative and satisfaction.
summary_en.result: The PBL group showed significantly higher scores in autonomous learning, active participation, and critical thinking.
summary_en.validation: Statistical comparison between experimental and control groups.
